notesStmt.note: Horace Traubel's notes for his visit to Whitman on 10 June 1889 suggest that the message written on the reverse of this manuscript was addressed to James Gordon Bennett, the editor of the New York Herald. He reports that a letter to Bennett lay on the table, containing "a poemet—a little conceit—suggested by the Exposition," for which Whitman was asking ten dollars. For whatever reason, the poem was not printed in the Herald. (See With Walt Whitman in Camden [Carbondale: Southern Illinois University Press, 1964] 5:280).
"Bravo, Paris Exposition!" was first published in Harper's Weekly on 28 September 1889 and reprinted, with a few changes in punctuation, in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891).

lg.head: Bravo, Paris Exhibition!
lg.l: Add to your show, dear France,

With all the rest, visible, concrete,
temples, towers, goods, machines
and ores,

Our sentiment, wafted from many million
heart-throbs, ethereal but solid,

(We grand-sons and great-grand-sons
do not forget your grand-sires.)

From fifty Nations and nebulous
Nations, compacted, sent, ‸oversea to-day,

America's applause, love, memories
and good-will.
